Note::TexAccessor::strip_tables¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::strip_tables() const

Remove Complete Table Structures¶

strip_tables() removes complete environments named table, table*, tabular, tabular*, longtable, or array. It is intended for source cleanup where tabular structures, captions inside them, and all cell content must disappear as one region. Use tables() when those structures should be extracted instead, or strip_env(name) when only one caller-selected environment kind should be removed.

The scanner balances nested environments as a stack, including heterogeneous nesting such as a tabular inside a table. Removing an accepted outer region therefore consumes that whole region once; a standalone accepted inner region is removed independently. Environment names are exact and case-sensitive. Escaped openers and incomplete or mismatched regions remain unchanged because silently deleting an unterminated remainder would lose authored source.

Each removed region contributes a separator, after which ASCII whitespace is collapsed and the cell is trimmed. A cell containing only a table becomes an empty string; it is not removed from the Note. The operation allocates a new Text Note, preserves rank and shape, leaves the receiver unchanged, and is idempotent. Undefined state propagates; defined non-Text input rejects. Runtime is linear in source bytes, with stack memory proportional to maximum environment nesting depth.

Example 1: Nested And Standalone Table Families¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(before \begin{table}outer \begin{tabular}x\end{tabular} tail\end{table} after)",
    R"(x \begin{array}a\end{array} y \begin{longtable}b\end{longtable} z)",
    R"(\\begin{table}escaped\\end{table} \begin{table}unfinished)"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_tables() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["before after", "x y z", "\\\\begin{table}escaped\\\\end{table} \\begin{table}unfinished"]

Example 2: Empty Results Preserve Matrix Position¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\begin{tabular}a\end{tabular})", "plain",
                             R"(x \begin{table*}b\end{table*} y)", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().strip_tables() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["", "plain"],
  ["x y", ""]
]

Example 3: Idempotence, Undefined State, And Dtype¶

const auto once = pluss::make_note(
    R"(a \begin{table}b\end{table} c)").tex().strip_tables();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "idempotent="
          << ((once == once.tex().strip_tables()).all().bool_item())
          << " undefined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_tables().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().strip_tables();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip tables Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

idempotent=true undefined=false
strip tables Int64: rejected
